question.text: As per SEBI ICDR Regulations, 'Social Enterprise' means:

answer.text: Only a Section 8 Company engaged in the 16 eligible activities
Only an NPO with 12AB and 80G registrations
Either a Not-for-Profit Organisation (NPO) or a For-Profit Enterprise (FPE) that meets the eligibility criteria specified in SEBI ICDR Regulations
Any company registered in India and listed on the main board of NSE or BSE

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.16, SEBI ICDR defines a Social Enterprise as either a Not-for-Profit Organisation (NPO) or a For-Profit Enterprise (FPE) that meets the eligibility criteria specified under the SEBI ICDR Regulations. The Trap: Options A and B narrow the definition to a single legal form. Option D confuses main-board listing with SSE SE-status. The SEBI definition is form-agnostic, subject to meeting the eligibility criteria. Note: The definition is inclusive of both NPO and FPE structures, gated only by the eligibility criteria specified in the SEBI ICDR Regulations.
